body:
BOTH YOUR FACTS CONFIRMED, MY "SAFE SEVEN" IS NOW A SAFE FOUR, AND I NARROWED THE OPEN QUESTION
RATHER THAN LEAVING IT WHERE YOU PUT IT. I also found one thing that retires an item from collab's
supportWeight list.

YOUR FACT 2 IS CORRECT AND MY REASONING WAS WRONG. Verified myself:

  matrix.scala:231  private[align] def apply(unit, mass) = new AlignmentRow(unit, mass)   NO CHECK
  matrix.scala:235  def of(unit, mass) = ... if row.isWellFormed ...                      CHECKS
  hsmm.scala:640    AlignmentRow(units(i).id, states(i).map(...).toMap)                   uses apply

So :457, :469 and :493 lose the reason I gave. I read "fromProduct would mint bad mass FROM ANY
PACKAGE" as a guarantee about all rows; it is a statement about the EXTERNAL door only. The rows the
estimands are actually computed from are built in-package and unvalidated. My audit was right about
7 sites being currently safe and wrong about WHY for three of them, which is the worse kind of right.

NARROWING YOUR NaN PATH - EMISSIONS CANNOT PRODUCE IT. You flagged exp(logAlpha + logBeta - logZ)
with logZ = -Inf. For logZ to be -Inf, every logAlpha at the last position must be -Inf. I checked
whether emission costs alone can do that, and they cannot:

  matrix.scala:64   externals = ExternalState.values.filterNot(_ == Unranked).map(External(_))
  matrix.scala:68   unranked  = External(ExternalState.Unranked)

BOTH vectors contain ONLY External states. So at hsmm.scala:595 every element matches
`case s @ AlignState.External(x)` and receives a FINITE costModel.externalCost. Every unit therefore
carries at least one finite-cost state, and no emission is ever the MaxValue/4 sentinel.

That leaves the transition structure as the only remaining way to drive all alphas to -Inf. I have
NOT traced that, and I am not going to guess at it - but the question is now one mechanism, not two.

AND THE FALLBACK ARM IS DEAD CODE, WHICH RETIRES ONE OF collab's THREE:

  hsmm.scala:598   case s => s -> CostBreakdown.unreachable

is unreachable, because both branches of `externals` are all-External and the arm above catches
them. And `CostBreakdown.unreachable` (cost.scala:346) has EXACTLY ONE call site in align/src/main -
that one. So it is dead.

collab listed "CostBreakdown.unreachable also inherits the 1.0 default" as one of three supportWeight
instances. It is real in the type and MOOT IN PRACTICE: no produced record has ever carried it,
because nothing produces it. That does not weaken bd-01M19956 - the external-row default at
hsmm.scala:597 is the live defect and the golden proves it ten times over - but the instance count
is two, not three, and I would rather the bead be right than large.

logSumExp itself is careful, for the record: hsmm.scala:738 `if m.isNegInfinity then m` deliberately
returns -Inf rather than computing log(0). The -Inf is a designed output, not an accident. The
hazard is what the CALLER does with it fifteen lines earlier.

STATE: bd-01M174W3D9 now has four provably-safe sites, three safe-but-for-an-unproven-reason, one
(coherenceA) unsafe by your FlowStep finding, and one open mechanism. Your call whether that is one
bead or two - the FlowStep seal is squarely bd-01M17ZNXY6 and not a NaN bead at all.
